lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Put the Harbor Payments internship before Crestline in Experience.
items.because: The section is not in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Make the profile link a clickable, complete URL.
Confirm the contact information is current, unless it has been anonymized.
Provide context for the diesel mechanic role or make the product experience more prominent without obscuring current employment.
items.because: The role immediately after an MBA and product internship may leave product recruiters unsure of your direction.

items.says: Clarify the basis for “under 5 days per job,” including the number of jobs or a benchmark if available.
items.because: That would make the claim easier to assess.

items.says: Specify the result of the maintenance or recordkeeping if you can support it.
items.because: The bullet describes responsibilities but not their effect.

items.says: Clarify what you owned beyond preparing carrier scorecards.
items.because: The bullet otherwise reads as routine reporting.

items.says: Explain what decisions or operational changes the review meetings enabled.
items.because: The bullet is the least specific Crestline bullet.

items.says: Add the measurement period or baseline for the pick-error reduction if known.
items.because: Readers could better judge the reduction’s size and durability.

items.says: Clarify how forecast error was measured or over what period.
Separate or prioritize the contributions in the route-planning bullet.
items.because: Combining rollout, procedures, training and negotiations makes the main achievement less immediately apparent.

items.says: Clarify how the 1,800 annual driver hours saved were measured.
Clarify whether the hours saved were across three depots or the wider region.
Clarify what “time to first payment” measures.
items.because: Readers need to interpret the change.

items.says: Give the pilot’s timeframe if available.
items.because: Readers need to interpret the result’s scope.

items.says: State the test duration or statistical-confidence context if available.
Make clear that the conversion change is five percentage points, not a relative five-percent increase.
Defining RICE Reach as support tickets closed suggests the metric was defined incorrectly.
items.because: Reach generally counts users or customers affected over a defined period; tickets closed may only be a proxy.

items.says: Include what prioritization resulted from the RICE scoring.
Distinguish the research and analysis from the RICE bullet’s prioritization work.
items.because: The two bullets overlap.

items.says: Make the resulting roadmap decision more concrete.
items.because: “Set the next quarter’s roadmap priority” does not say what changed.

items.says: The A/B-test bullet repeats the checkout-conversion result in the earlier bullet.
items.because: The space could show a distinct contribution instead.

items.says: Clarify what “effect on merchants’ customers” means.
items.because: The measured outcome should be unmistakable.

items.says: Clarify whether funding was approved, the rollout happened, or both.
Quantify the rollout’s impact if results from the additional regions are available.
Clarify whether 3,100 students were reached, registered or eligible to use the app.
items.because: “Launched … to” leaves the measure open to interpretation.

items.says: The stated 150% weekly-active-user increase is incorrect for a rise from 400 to 1,150.
items.because: A 750-user increase from 400 is 187.5%.

items.says: Clarify the weekly-active-user measurement period.
Clarify whether the interviews directly informed the reminder feature.
The move from 75% to 95% is not a 20% increase.
items.because: It is a 20-percentage-point increase, or about a 26.7% relative increase.

items.says: Specify the pickup-slot comparison period if available.
Make clear that the $2.4M annual saving is modeled or projected unless implementation has confirmed it.
items.because: Readers might interpret an estimate as a delivered result.

items.says: Use active wording to clarify what you personally did.
items.because: The passive construction obscures your role.

items.says: Specify what changed, such as the form reduction or a measured operational outcome.
items.because: The result is vague.

items.says: The pilot-approval outcome repeats the first practicum bullet.
items.because: The approval evidence should appear once unless the bullets describe different decisions or stages.

items.says: Emphasize the resulting decision or implementation rather than the presentation itself.
items.because: The presentation is less valuable than its outcome.

items.says: Use the skills section for additional relevant capabilities you can substantiate.
items.because: Much of the current list is already demonstrated in Experience.

items.says: Add other tools you can use confidently if they fit the target roles.
items.because: The tools list is short.
